A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GaussianFusion. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including relocated tables and the new Appendix D.

before.justification: v1 reports original NAVSIM and Bench2Drive experiments, component ablations, fusion comparisons, and hyperparameter studies in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and reports additional backbone results, an additional ablation, three-seed Bench2Drive results, and qualitative failure cases.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same Gaussian initialization, dual-branch fusion, refinement, cascade planning, and losses. V2-99 is an additional evaluated backbone configuration; no new fusion or planning procedure is introduced.

E1.justification: NAVSIM/OpenScene and Bench2Drive remain the benchmarks for the same driving tasks. Qualitative scenario coverage expands through Appendix D, particularly the explicit low-visibility/fog example in Figure 6(b); no additional dataset or quantitative weather benchmark is reported.

E2.justification: The standard-PDMS comparison expands within the Hydra family. The 86.5-PDMS row labeled Hydra-MDP++ in v1 Table 5 is labeled Hydra-MDP in v2 Table 1, alongside a separate camera-only Hydra-MDP++ row and a V2-99 Hydra-MDP-C entry. EPDMS and Bench2Drive comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds V2-99 evaluations and FLOPs reporting. Section 5 replaces v1's general three-camera, 448×250 description with a Bench2Drive-specific front-camera-only, 1024×384 setting. This is a reported protocol revision, without establishing whether earlier experiments were rerun. Existing splits, driving metrics, and training schedule are retained.

E4.justification: v2 Table 4 adds explicit fusion plus cascade planning without implicit fusion, isolating the cascade's contribution more clearly. Appendix D/Figure 6 adds turning, low-visibility, and following/overtaking failure cases. Existing component comparisons and Appendix C hyperparameter sweeps remain.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without seed counts. v2 Section 5.1 specifies three random seeds for Bench2Drive, and Table 3 adds ± quantities for TF++ and GaussianFusion. The uncertainty statistic is not explicitly defined, and the PDFs do not establish an increase from a known earlier run count.

E6.justification: v2 adds 92.0 PDMS for GaussianFusion with V2-99; the ResNet-34 table results remain 88.8 PDMS and 85.0 EPDMS. Bench2Drive DS entries change from 79.4 to 79.1±1.1 for GaussianFusion and 77.2 to 76.9±0.9 for TF++, under revised reporting/settings. Added results include the 84.4-EPDMS ablation, FLOPs, and failure examples. These are limited extensions and replacements, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–10, including Gaussian superposition and foreground/background reasoning in Appendix A, are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or formal assumption is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about Gaussian-based multi-sensor fusion, dual-branch features, cascade planning, and benchmark effectiveness. The introduction highlights the new V2-99 score, but the central contribution and superiority claims retain their meaning.

C2.justification: v2 substantially broadens the limitations beyond the retained CUDA-efficiency caveat. It identifies untested small/fast-object tracking and sensor occlusion/noise, plus costly annotation requirements. Appendix D introduces explanations involving conservative training priors, degraded Gaussian discrimination in fog, and uncertainty about other vehicles, qualifying applicability and driving efficiency.

D1.justification: v2 documents benchmark-specific camera inputs and resolutions, identifies the V2-99 configuration, and explicitly states dependence on bounding-box and road-topology labels. It removes v1's named TF++ training-data setting. Core hyperparameters, RTX3090 latency hardware, and the future code-release statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the MILE reference and a short explanation of its BEV construction, plus the backbone reference used for V2-99. The positioning against flatten fusion, BEV fusion, and GaussianAD remains substantially unchanged; other citation-number changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites update the introduction and experimental discussion, emphasizing standard PDMS before EPDMS. v2 adds a limitations paragraph, Appendix D, acknowledgments, and corresponding-author/conference text. The main narrative and method exposition remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v1's appendix PDMS table moves into the main text as v2 Table 1, expanded with backbone groups. v2 also adds an ablation row, a FLOPs column, uncertainty formatting, and Figure 6. Figures 1–5 retain their visual content, with caption styling and layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: Three-seed reporting, the additional controlled ablation, FLOPs accounting, and explicit failure cases make the existing empirical case more informative and better qualified. These gains are tempered by undefined ± statistics, removal of the explicit Bench2Drive training-data setting, and stale prose reporting 79.4 DS despite Table 3 showing 79.1±1.1. The net improvement is limited but supported.
